flashcards.back: P = √3 V_L I_L cos φ = 3 V_ph I_ph cos φ, where φ is the angle between phase voltage and phase current.

flashcards.front: What is phase sequence, and what happens if it is reversed?
flashcards.back: The order in which the three phase voltages reach their positive peaks, normally RYB. Interchanging any two lines reverses the sequence and a three-phase motor runs backwards.

questions.questionText: A balanced star-connected load is supplied from a 400 V (line) three-phase system. The voltage across each phase of the load is:
To reverse the direction of rotation of a three-phase induction motor, one should:
options: Shift all three supply lines one place round (R to Y, Y to B, B to R)
Reverse the connection of the neutral wire
Interchange any two of the three supply lines
questions.explanation: Swapping any two lines reverses the phase sequence and hence the rotating field; a cyclic shift keeps the same sequence.

questions.questionText: In a balanced delta-connected load the line current is 17.32 A. The current in each phase of the load is:
In a balanced three-phase, four-wire star system, the current in the neutral wire is:
questions.explanation: The three balanced line currents are equal and 120° apart, so their phasor sum, the neutral current, is zero.

questions.questionText: In a balanced star-connected load each phase carries 15 A. The line current is:
questions.explanation: In star each line is in series with its phase, so I_L = I_ph = 15 A.

questions.questionText: For positive phase sequence RYB in a star-connected system, the line voltage V_RY, compared with the phase voltage V_R:
questions.explanation: V_RY = V_R − V_Y = √3 V_ph∠30°, so the line voltage leads the corresponding phase voltage by 30°.

questions.questionText: A balanced delta-connected load is fed from a 400 V three-phase supply. The voltage across each phase of the load is:
questions.explanation: In delta each phase is connected directly between two lines, so V_ph = V_L = 400 V.

questions.questionText: A three-phase, four-wire supply providing both 400 V and 230 V requires the source windings to be connected in:
options: Star, with the neutral brought out
questions.explanation: Only a star connection has a neutral point; line-to-line gives 400 V and line-to-neutral gives 400/√3 = 230 V.

questions.questionText: A balanced three-phase load takes a line current of 10 A from a 400 V supply at a power factor of 0.8 lagging. The total active power is:
The total instantaneous power delivered to a balanced three-phase load is:
options: Pulsating at twice the supply frequency
Pulsating at three times the supply frequency
questions.explanation: The double-frequency pulsations of the three phases are 120° apart and cancel, leaving a constant 3 V_ph I_ph cos φ.

questions.questionText: A balanced three-phase load draws 50 A from a 400 V supply at a power factor of 0.6 lagging. The total reactive power is:
In the expression P = √3 V_L I_L cos φ for a balanced load, φ is the phase angle between:
questions.explanation: φ is the load impedance angle, the angle between each phase voltage and its phase current; the angle between line voltage and line current is (30° ± φ).

questions.questionText: A balanced three-phase motor takes 10 kW from a 400 V supply at a power factor of 0.85 lagging. The line current is:
In the two-wattmeter method on a balanced load, one wattmeter gives a negative (reversed) reading. This shows that the load power factor is:
questions.explanation: W2 = V_L I_L cos(30° + φ) becomes negative when φ exceeds 60°, i.e. when cos φ < 0.5.

questions.questionText: Three identical 10 Ω resistors are connected in star across a 400 V, three-phase supply. The total power consumed is:
questions.explanation: V_ph = 400/√3 = 231 V; P = 3 × V_ph²/R = 3 × 231²/10 = 16.0 kW (equivalently V_L²/R).

questions.questionText: Three identical 10 Ω resistors are connected in delta across a 400 V, three-phase supply. The line current is:
Two wattmeters measure the power of a balanced, purely inductive three-phase load. Their readings will be:
options: Equal in magnitude but opposite in sign
One zero and the other positive
questions.explanation: With φ = 90°: W1 = V_L I_L cos(−60°) = +0.5 V_L I_L and W2 = V_L I_L cos 120° = −0.5 V_L I_L, so the total is zero.

questions.questionText: A balanced star load with Z = 6 + j8 Ω per phase is connected to a 400 V, three-phase supply. The total active power is:
A balanced delta load with Z = 8 + j6 Ω per phase is connected to a 400 V, three-phase supply. The line current and the power factor are:
Which of the following is NOT an advantage of a three-phase system over a single-phase system?
options: Power delivered to a balanced load is constant rather than pulsating
Less conductor material is needed to transmit the same power
Two different voltages can be obtained from one four-wire supply
Three-phase induction motors need a separate auxiliary winding to start
questions.explanation: Three-phase windings produce a rotating field, so three-phase induction motors are self-starting; an auxiliary starting winding is needed by single-phase motors.

questions.questionText: Two wattmeters connected to measure the power of a balanced three-phase load read 3 kW and 1 kW. The power factor of the load is:
In the two-wattmeter method the readings are W1 = 6 kW and W2 = −1 kW (the second meter had to be reversed). The total power is:
questions.explanation: P = W1 + W2 = 6 + (−1) = 5 kW; a reversed reading must be subtracted.

questions.questionText: A balanced delta-connected resistive load is supplied at constant line voltage. If one phase resistor goes open-circuit, the total power becomes:
questions.explanation: The other two resistors still each see the full line voltage and draw their original power, so 2 of the 3 equal phase powers remain.

questions.questionText: A balanced load of power factor 0.5 lagging takes a total of 8 kW, measured by the two-wattmeter method. The two wattmeter readings are:
questions.explanation: At cos φ = 0.5, φ = 60°: W2 = V_L I_L cos 90° = 0, so W1 carries the whole 8 kW.

questions.questionText: A balanced load with power factor 0.866 lagging takes a total of 9 kW, measured by two wattmeters. The individual readings are:
questions.explanation: φ = 30°: W1 = V_L I_L cos 0° and W2 = V_L I_L cos 60° = W1/2; W1 + W2 = 1.5 W1 = 9 kW gives W1 = 6 kW, W2 = 3 kW.

questions.questionText: A three-phase, three-wire supply feeds an unbalanced star-connected load with no neutral wire. Which statement is correct?
options: The star point of the load shifts from the supply neutral, so the three phase voltages become unequal
The three phase voltages stay equal to V_L/√3 because the line voltages are balanced
The line currents are still equal, only their phase angles change
The load draws no current until a neutral wire is connected
questions.explanation: Without a neutral, unequal impedances move the load star point (neutral shift); the line voltages stay balanced but the phase voltages and currents become unequal.

questions.questionText: A star-connected three-phase system has a line voltage of 11 kV. The phase (line-to-neutral) voltage is:
A delta-connected induction motor takes a starting line current of 60 A when switched direct-on-line. If a star-delta starter is used on the same supply, the starting line current is:
questions.explanation: In star each winding gets V_L/√3, so I_ph falls by √3 and I_L = I_ph (not √3 I_ph); overall the line current is one third: 60/3 = 20 A.

questions.questionText: The minimum number of wattmeters needed to measure the total power of an unbalanced three-phase, four-wire load is:
questions.explanation: By Blondel's theorem the number needed is one fewer than the number of wires: 4 − 1 = 3.

questions.questionText: A balanced delta-connected heater load takes 15 kW from a 400 V, three-phase supply at unity power factor. The current in each phase of the heater is:
questions.explanation: Power per phase = 15/3 = 5 kW; V_ph = V_L = 400 V; I_ph = 5000/400 = 12.5 A (the line current would be √3 × 12.5 = 21.7 A).

questions.questionText: The phasor sum of the three phase voltages of a balanced three-phase supply is:
questions.explanation: Three equal phasors 120° apart form a closed triangle, so their sum is zero at every instant.

questions.questionText: A balanced star-connected load takes 20 kW from a 400 V, three-phase supply at 0.8 power factor lagging. The magnitude of the impedance of each phase is:
A delta-connected induction motor is started with a star-delta starter. Compared with direct-on-line starting in delta, the starting torque is:
questions.explanation: Torque is proportional to the square of the winding voltage; in star it is V_L/√3, so torque falls to (1/√3)² = 1/3.

questions.questionText: A 400 V, three-phase, four-wire system supplies unity power factor loads in star drawing 20 A, 20 A and 10 A in lines R, Y and B respectively. The neutral current is:
questions.explanation: Phasor sum: 20∠0° + 20∠−120° + 10∠120° = (balanced 20 A set, sum 0) − 10∠120°, whose magnitude is 10 A.

questions.questionText: Which statement about a balanced delta connection is NOT correct?
options: The line voltage equals the phase voltage
The line current is √3 times the phase current
Each line current leads the corresponding phase current by 30°
questions.explanation: In a delta connection each line current lags (not leads) the corresponding phase current by 30°; the other three statements are true.

questions.questionText: At a certain instant in a balanced three-phase, three-wire system, i_R = 10 A and i_Y = −4 A. The instantaneous current i_B at that instant is:
questions.explanation: The three instantaneous line currents of a 3-wire system sum to zero: i_B = −(10 − 4) = −6 A.

questions.questionText: Two wattmeters measuring a balanced three-phase load read 5 kW and 3 kW. The total reactive power of the load is:
For the same power, distance, voltage between lines and line loss, a three-phase three-wire line needs, compared with a single-phase two-wire line:
questions.explanation: Three-phase transmission needs only about three quarters of the copper of a single-phase line for the same power and losses.

questions.questionText: Three identical 20 Ω resistors are connected in star (no neutral) across a 400 V, three-phase supply. If one resistor goes open-circuit, the total power consumed becomes:
questions.explanation: The remaining two resistors are in series across the 400 V line: P = V_L²/(2R) = 400²/40 = 4.00 kW, half of the original 8 kW.

questions.questionText: A three-phase, 100 kVA transformer has a secondary line voltage of 400 V. Its full-load secondary line current is:
With the phase sequence RYB and V_R taken as V∠0°, the phase voltage V_B is:
questions.explanation: V_Y lags V_R by 120° and V_B lags by 240°, which is the same as leading by 120°, so V_B = V∠+120°.

questions.questionText: A balanced delta-connected load on a 400 V, three-phase supply carries 10 A in each phase at a power factor of 0.7 lagging. The total active power is:
questions.explanation: P = 3 V_ph I_ph cos φ = 3 × 400 × 10 × 0.7 = 8.40 kW (V_ph = V_L in delta).

questions.questionText: A balanced three-phase load on a 400 V supply gives two-wattmeter readings of 4 kW and 2 kW. The line current is:
Each phase of a balanced three-phase load takes 2 kW and 1.5 kVAR. The total apparent power of the load is:
questions.explanation: Per phase S = √(2² + 1.5²) = 2.5 kVA; total S = 3 × 2.5 = 7.5 kVA (total P = 6 kW, Q = 4.5 kVAR).

questions.questionText: In a 50 Hz three-phase system, the time interval between the positive peaks of two successive phase voltages is:
questions.explanation: The phases are 120° = one third of a cycle apart: T/3 = (1/50)/3 = 6.67 ms.

questions.questionText: The phase sequence of a three-phase supply is the:
options: Angle of 120° between any two phase voltages
Order in which the three phase voltages reach their positive maximum values
Ratio of line voltage to phase voltage
Order in which the phase windings are placed round the alternator stator
questions.explanation: Phase sequence (normally RYB) is the order in which the phase voltages attain their positive peaks; 120° is the phase displacement, not the sequence.
